winterPackages.name: FreezeGuard
includes: Drain engine block and manifolds; fill with non-toxic antifreeze
Fog engine, add fuel stabilizer, remove drain plug(s)
Inspect and check lower-unit gear lube

winterPackages.name: SystemShield
includes: Change engine oil, oil filter and fuel filter (up to 6 qt oil)
Drain, inspect and refill gear lube (trailer or lift only)

winterPackages.name: TotalLock
includes: Grease U-joints, seals and bearings on the drive system
Change impeller; inspect water pump and gasket
20-point full vessel inspection with a written summary

winterPackages.name: SecurePro
includes: 6 months of secure, uncovered storage at our service center

outboardMenu.name: 2-stroke basic
outboardMenu.note: Add fuel treatment, check all fluid levels, inspect lower-unit gear lube.

outboardMenu.name: 4-stroke basic
outboardMenu.note: Add fuel treatment, check fluids, inspect gear lube and lower-unit seals.

outboardMenu.name: 4-stroke enhanced
outboardMenu.note: Fuel treatment, engine oil and filter change, inspect gear lube and lower unit.

outboardMenu.name: 4-stroke ultimate
outboardMenu.note: Full oil and filter service, drain and refill gear lube, 20-point vessel inspection. Trailer or lift only.

outboardMenu.name: PWC (Jet Ski, Sea-Doo, WaveRunner)
outboardMenu.note: Stabilize fuel, clear water from the jet drive and engine, run and fill the block with non-toxic antifreeze.

addOns.name: Dewinterization (spring startup)
addOns.note: Flush antifreeze, reconnect systems, verify operation. Required for the winterization guarantee.

addOns.name: Freshwater or ballast system
addOns.note: Drain and fill with non-toxic antifreeze.

addOns.name: Blackwater (holding tanks)
addOns.note: Tank must be empty on arrival.

addOns.name: Shrink wrap
addOns.note: White wrap with vents and supports. Done at our service center.

addOns.name: Uncovered storage
addOns.note: Secure outdoor storage for shrink-wrapped boats.

addOns.name: Extra motors, generator, AC, shower, fridge
addOns.note: Billed at labor rate, materials extra.

winterNotes: All package pricing is labor only, for single-engine boats. Materials (antifreeze, oil, filters, stabilizer, parts) are billed separately, and we won't do additional work without an estimate first.

scout.heroAlt: A Scout center console running fast across open water
scout.differenceIntro: For over 25 years, Scout Boats has built a reputation on one simple promise: to create the finest fishing and family boats on the water. Every Scout combines offshore capability, tournament-grade fishability, and family-friendly comfort in a package that’s built to last generations. This isn’t marketing—it’s South Carolina craftsmanship backed by passionate anglers who refuse to compromise.

points.title: Offshore Confidence
points.body: Deep-V hulls with 20-24 degree deadrise deliver smooth, dry rides in rough water. From Lake Texoma chop to Gulf Coast swells, Scout hulls inspire confidence wherever you point the bow.

points.title: Tournament Ready
points.body: Massive insulated fish boxes, dozens of rodholders, raw-water washdowns, and tackle storage everywhere. Scout’s fishing features aren’t afterthoughts—they’re designed by anglers who live on the water.

points.title: Family Comfort
points.body: Premium upholstery, spacious lounges, optional cabin berths, and head compartments. Scout doesn’t make you choose between fishing and family—you get both in one incredible package.

points.title: South Carolina Craftsmanship
points.body: Hand-laid fiberglass, wood-free construction, premium gelcoat, and obsessive attention to detail. Every Scout is built in Summerville, SC by craftsmen who take pride in their work.

points.title: Power Matched Performance
points.body: Scout partners with Yamaha, Mercury, and Suzuki for unmatched reliability and performance. From efficient four-strokes to screaming V8s, Scout’s outboard options deliver the perfect balance of speed, fuel economy, and dependability.

points.title: Award-Winning Innovation
points.body: Multiple NMMA Innovation Awards and BoatTest.com “Best Of” honors. Scout consistently pushes the boundaries with features like LXF luxury sport yachts, hydraulic platforms, and industry-leading storage solutions.

scout.videoBody: Experience the legendary Scout ride, tournament-grade fishing features, and family-friendly comfort that makes Scout the choice of serious boaters. Watch reviews, walkthroughs, and real-world performance on Scout’s YouTube channel.
scout.fleetIntro: From versatile bay boats to luxury sport fishing yachts, Scout builds boats for every adventure. Whether you’re chasing bass on Lake Texoma or heading offshore in the Gulf, there’s a Scout built for your style of boating.

series.name: Dorado Series
series.body: The ultimate family fishing boats. Dual console protection, massive fishing features, comfortable seating, and legendary Scout ride quality. Perfect for families who fish seriously.

series.name: LXF Series
series.body: Where luxury meets tournament performance. Air conditioning, cabin berths, premium entertainment systems, and every fishing feature imaginable. The pinnacle of Scout engineering.

series.name: XSF Series
series.body: Pure fishing machines with serious offshore capability. Tournament-grade features, massive fuel capacity, and hardcore fishing layouts for anglers who demand the best.

series.name: Sport Series
series.body: The gateway to Scout ownership. Smaller packages with big boat features—fishing amenities, comfortable seating, and that unmistakable Scout ride.

series.name: Bay Series
series.body: Shallow water specialists built for inshore fishing. Lightweight, nimble, and loaded with fishing features. Perfect for Texas bays, Louisiana marshes, or Lake Texoma’s countless coves.

scout.whyIntro: As Lake Texoma’s factory-authorized Scout dealer, we provide the complete ownership experience—from expert sales consultation to factory-authorized Yamaha service. We’re passionate Scout owners ourselves, and we’re here to ensure your Scout ownership is exceptional.

whyUs.title: Warranty Experts
whyUs.body: Official Scout dealer with direct factory support and comprehensive warranty backing. We handle all warranty work efficiently and correctly.

whyUs.title: Factory-Authorized Service
whyUs.body: Expert marine technicians keep your Scout running at peak performance. We know these boats inside and out.

whyUs.title: White-Glove Delivery
whyUs.body: Complete rigging, sea trials, on-site training, and walkthrough. Your Scout arrives perfect and ready for adventure.

whyUs.title: Lifetime Support
whyUs.body: You’re not just buying a boat—you’re joining the Big Water Marine family. We’re here for you throughout your entire Scout ownership journey.

faqs.q: What makes Scout boats different from other brands?
faqs.a: Scout Boats combines offshore capability, tournament-grade fishing features, and family comfort in every model. Built in South Carolina with hand-laid fiberglass and wood-free construction, Scout boats are designed by anglers who understand what serious boaters need. The exclusive Yamaha partnership ensures reliable, efficient power, while award-winning innovations keep Scout at the forefront of boat design.

faqs.q: Are Scout boats good for Lake Texoma?
faqs.a: Absolutely. Scout’s deep-V hulls handle Lake Texoma’s chop with ease, delivering smooth, dry rides even in rough conditions. The versatile layouts work perfectly for Texas striped bass fishing, family days on the lake, and everything in between. Scout’s superior build quality stands up to the rigors of freshwater use while maintaining that legendary Scout ride.

faqs.q: What warranty comes with a new Scout?
faqs.a: New Scout boats come with a comprehensive manufacturer warranty covering structure, components, and gelcoat. Each motor manufacturer carries separate factory warranties. As a factory-authorized dealer, Big Water Marine handles all warranty service directly, ensuring fast, professional repairs.

faqs.q: Can you finance a Scout purchase?
faqs.a: Yes! We offer competitive marine financing with terms up to 20 years and rates as low as 5.99% APR for qualified buyers. We work with multiple marine lenders to secure the best rate and structure for your situation.

faqs.q: What's a quick overview of the Scout models?
faqs.a: Scout Boats builds a range of models designed to fit every style of boating, from shallow-water fishing to offshore luxury cruising. The LXS and LXF series sit at the top—premium, high-performance center consoles and sport yachts with advanced materials, elegant finishes, and offshore range. The XSF (Sportfish) line delivers similar performance in a more fishing-focused package, balancing speed and versatility. The Dorado series features dual-console layouts ideal for families who split their time between cruising and casual fishing, while the Bay Boat (XSS/XSB) models are shallow-draft designs built for lakes, bays, and inshore adventures. Together, the lineup combines Scout’s signature quality, innovation, and style across every size and price point.

faqs.q: What makes Veranda different from other pontoons?
faqs.a: The patented, all-aluminum, interlocking deck system. It’s rigid, quiet, and eliminates wood that can rot—giving you a solid, long-lasting platform with premium comfort.

faqs.q: Are Veranda pontoons good for Lake Texoma?
faqs.a: Yes—solid ride, stable platforms, and versatile layouts make Veranda ideal for Texoma’s chop, coves, and all-day family cruising.

faqs.q: What motor options are available with Veranda?
faqs.a: Veranda Luxury Pontoons are matched exclusively with Yamaha Outboard for the most reliable motor.

faqs.q: What warranty comes with a new Veranda?
faqs.a: Manufacturer warranties apply to structure and components, with separate factory warranties for outboards. As an authorized dealer, we handle warranty service in-house.

faqs.q: Can you finance a Veranda purchase?
faqs.a: Absolutely. We work with leading marine lenders to secure competitive rates and terms up to 20 years for qualified buyers.

faqs.q: What layouts and power options are available?
faqs.a: Veranda’s layout codes make it easy to find your perfect pontoon setup. The F (Fish) layouts include fishing seats and livewells for anglers, while the RC (Rear Chase) offers aft-facing loungers ideal for relaxing and sunning. The VL (Versa Lounger) provides multi-position rear seating that converts from bench to sun pad, and the L (L-Shaped Lounger) maximizes space for entertaining and conversation. Models with P feature plush Pillow-Top Seating for added luxury and comfort, and DC (Dual Console) designs add a sportier look and improved wind protection for the captain and co-captain.

faqs.q: What's the difference between the Vista, Relax, Vertex and V-One series?
faqs.a: The Vista Series offers exceptional value by combining Veranda’s patented all-aluminum deck system with upscale styling in compact 20′–22′ or 25′ formats—ideal for families starting out on Lake Texoma. The Relax Series steps things up with chaise lounges, upgraded dashboards and lighting options, blending lounge-style comfort and casual performance. The Vertex Series brings luxury and performance together—with premium furniture, fiberglass console accents and refined finishes for those who demand refinement in addition to function. And the flagship V One Series pushes maximum performance and style, featuring a tri-toon layout with striking fiberglass exterior, high-end audio and electronics, and twin-engine capability for serious lake-life luxury.

highfield.differenceIntro: When you’re investing in a premium rigid inflatable boat, you need more than promises—you need proof. Highfield RIBs have earned their reputation as America’s best-selling RIB brand through relentless engineering, uncompromising quality, and a commitment to pushing the boundaries of what’s possible on the water.

points.title: Proven Performance
points.body: From 10′ yacht tenders to 30′ offshore machines, Highfield delivers speeds up to 60 mph with confidence. Dry-riding hulls, superior seaworthiness, and handling that inspires you to explore further.

points.title: Aluminum Advantage
points.body: Forget gel coat chips and hull delamination. Highfield’s powder-coated aluminum hulls are eco-friendly, recyclable, and virtually indestructible. Beach your boat without worry—these hulls can take whatever you throw at them.

points.title: Luxury Refinement
points.body: EVA teak decking, diamond-stitch upholstery, and integrated LED lighting create the most sophisticated RIB on the water. Recessed stainless-steel cleats, premium helm consoles—every detail refined.

points.title: ORCA Hypalon Tubes
points.body: Premium tube construction using German Valmex PVC or French ORCA Hypalon for extreme durability. UV-resistant, chemical-resistant, and backed by warranties up to 10 years.

points.title: Integrated Fuel Tanks
points.body: Every Sport Series model features clean, integrated fuel tanks—maximizing deck space and maintaining the sleek aesthetic. No portable tanks cluttering your cockpit.

points.title: Military-Grade Construction
points.body: High-tensile aluminum hulls built to commercial Patrol series standards. 20-26 degree deadrise for superior handling in rough water. When Coast Guard professionals choose Highfield for search and rescue, you know these boats are built to last.

highfield.videoBody: The Best Selling RIB in the US, but don’t take our word for it, learn more on Highfield’s YouTube page. Best in class design, performance, and construction and absolutely fun.
highfield.fleetIntro: From compact 10-foot tenders to 30-foot offshore command centers, Highfield builds a RIB for every adventure. Every model shares the same DNA: military-grade construction, luxury refinement, and performance that exceeds expectations.

series.name: Sport Series
series.body: The flagship series. Premium yacht tenders and day boats featuring upscale styling, EVA teak decking, and diamond-stitch upholstery.

series.name: Classic Console Series
series.body: Lightweight performance meets console convenience. Perfect combination of early planing, durability, and amazing space in a compact RIB.

series.name: Velox Jet Series
series.body: The future of family boating. Rotax jet propulsion delivers instant throttle response, shallow water access, and virtually zero maintenance.

series.name: Patrol Series
series.body: When response, safety, and handling matter, the Patrol Series is ideal. Designed with First Responders, Law Enforcement, and Commercial Operators in mind. Big Water Marine specializes in building boats for response and rescue operations.

highfield.whyIntro: As Lake Texoma’s factory-authorized Highfield dealer, we don’t just sell boats—we provide a complete ownership experience backed by expertise, service, and genuine care.

faqs.q: What makes Highfield RIBs different from other brands?
faqs.a: Highfield RIBs feature military-grade aluminum hulls that are powder-coated and built to commercial Patrol series standards. Unlike fiberglass hulls, you never have to worry about gel coat chips, stress cracks, or delamination. Combined with premium Orca Hypalon tubes, EVA teak decking, and luxury appointments, Highfield delivers unmatched durability with sophisticated style.

faqs.q: Are Highfield boats good for Lake Texoma?
faqs.a: Absolutely. Highfield RIBs excel in the varied conditions of Lake Texoma—from calm coves to choppy main-lake runs. The 20-26 degree deadrise hulls provide excellent rough-water handling, while the shallow draft and RIB tube design make them perfect for beach landings and tight marina maneuvering.

faqs.q: What's the warranty on a new Highfield?

faqs.q: Can you finance a Highfield purchase?

faqs.q: What engine options are available?
faqs.a: Highfield RIBs can be rigged with Mercury, Yamaha, Suzuki, or BRP outboards depending on model and your preferences. The Velox series features Rotax jet propulsion. We’ll help you select the perfect power package based on your intended use.

faqs.q: Are Berkshire pontoons good for Lake Texoma?
faqs.a: Absolutely—Berkshire’s performance toons handle Texoma’s chop with ease while offering the comfort and versatility families love for cruising, watersports, and entertaining.

faqs.q: Can you finance a Berkshire?
faqs.a: Yes, we offer competitive marine financing with flexible terms and quick approvals to make your Berkshire ownership effortless.

faqs.q: What are the differences of the models (LE, CTS, STS, Sport)?
faqs.a: Berkshire offers four distinct series to fit every boater’s lifestyle. The LE Series delivers exceptional value with quality construction and classic styling—perfect for families and first-time pontoon owners. The CTS Series adds upscale features, enhanced performance options, and refined comfort for those who want a step up in luxury. The STS Series represents Berkshire’s premium line, combining top-tier materials, cutting-edge technology, and superior ride quality for an uncompromising experience. Finally, the Sport Series is the boldest of all, merging luxury and performance with sleek, athletic styling, advanced helm systems, and performance-tuned handling for those who want to make every day on the water exhilarating.

home.q: Do you service boats you didn’t sell?

home.q: Can you come to my boat?

home.q: Can routine service really be done the same day?
home.a: Often, with advance scheduling. Oil, filter, impeller and other factory-interval work depends on parts, workload and your boat. We’ll confirm timing with you up front.

inventory.q: Do your boat prices include the trailer?

inventory.q: What isn’t included in the listed price?

Yes. Get a quick estimate with our online trade tool; the final value is set after we see the boat in person.

inventory.q: Can you deliver a boat outside Lake Texoma?
inventory.a: Yes. We offer reasonable delivery anywhere in the U.S., and every boat we sell gets a lake-ready orientation.

inventory.q: What does “On order” mean on a listing?
inventory.a: The boat is built or being built and on its way to us. You can reserve it now so it’s yours when it arrives.

inventory.q: Can I finance a boat with you?
inventory.a: Yes. Apply online for fast, secure pre-approval. Each listing has a loan calculator so you can estimate a monthly payment first.

service.q: How do I schedule boat service at Big Water Marine?
service.a: Start a work order online through our secure service intake. It takes about two minutes. Our service team texts you back to confirm the work, the timing and the price, and texts again when your boat is ready. You can also call or text 903-419-1019.

service.q: Do you service boats you didn’t sell?
service.a: Yes. We’re factory-authorized for Suzuki, Yamaha, Mercury and BRP, and we service all major outboards plus sterndrives (I/O), wherever the boat came from.

service.q: Can routine maintenance be done the same day?

service.q: Do you offer mobile boat service on Lake Texoma?
service.a: Yes. Our mobile team comes to marinas, docks, storage facilities and homes around Lake Texoma, and we’re an approved, insured vendor at most marinas from Highport to Rock Creek and Cedar Bayou. Mobile labor is ${labor.mobile}/hour plus travel (${mobileTravel.minimum} minimum, ${mobileTravel.perMile}/mile). Some work, like gear lube or impeller changes, needs the boat on a trailer or lift.
${labor.onsite} per hour at our Pottsboro service center and ${labor.mobile} per hour for mobile service, plus parts and materials. We give you an estimate before doing additional work.

service.q: Will service at Big Water Marine keep my engine warranty intact?
service.a: Yes. As an authorized service center for Mercury, Yamaha, Suzuki and BRP, we follow factory procedures, use genuine OEM parts and fluids, and have direct manufacturer support.

service.q: Can you pick up my boat?
service.a: Yes. We can pick your boat up, service it at our facility and bring it back. For on-water emergencies, we work with TowBoatUS Lake Texoma, then get you back out fast.

service.q: Where is the service center and what are the hours?
service.a: 33 Tackle Box Dr, Pottsboro, TX 75076, minutes from Lake Texoma. Open Tuesday through Friday 8am–5pm and Saturday 8am–3pm.

winterize.q: Why winterize my boat if Texas doesn’t get deep freezes?
winterize.a: While Texas winters are milder than up north, GEICO and BoatUS data show Texas ranks #1 nationally for freeze-damage insurance claims — mostly from owners who skipped winterization. Even a single cold night can cause water to expand and crack blocks, split hoses, or destroy cooling systems. Professional winterization protects your investment.

winterize.q: What’s the difference between your winterization packages?
winterize.a: Each builds on the last. FreezeGuard is essential freeze protection: drain, fog and stabilize. SystemShield adds oil, fuel filter and gear lube service. TotalLock adds a full mechanical inspection, impeller and a 20-point vessel check. SecurePro is all-in: shrink wrap, six months of storage and spring dewinterization.

winterize.q: What does the winterization guarantee cover?
winterize.a: If your engine doesn’t start in spring because of our winterization process, we make it right at no charge. The guarantee applies when Big Water Marine also performs your spring dewinterization, so we can verify the system end to end.

winterize.q: What is dewinterization and why does it matter?
winterize.a: Dewinterization is the spring startup: flushing antifreeze, reconnecting systems, checking for leaks and verifying everything works. It’s $165, included in SecurePro, and required for the guarantee.

winterize.q: Can you winterize my boat at a marina, storage facility or my house?
winterize.a: Yes. Our mobile team travels to marinas, storage facilities and homes across Lake Texoma. Mobile rates apply, plus travel ($75 minimum, $2.50 per mile). Gear lube and impeller work needs the boat on a trailer or lift.

winterize.q: Can I just use a marine heater or lamp instead?
winterize.a: While marine approved bilge heaters are a good idea, they aren’t a substitute for winterization. Power outages, tripped breakers, or temperature swings can still freeze and crack components. Many Texas freeze claims happen because heaters failed during sudden cold snaps or power outage.
{inspectionPoints}. You get a summary report with any recommended maintenance.

winterize.q: When should I book my winterization?
winterize.a: As early as possible — once temperatures dip, appointments fill quickly. We start scheduling in late summer, and prime weeks typically sell out. Don’t wait until the first freeze warning.

winterize.q: Are materials included in the price?
winterize.a: No. Package prices are labor only, for single-engine boats. Materials such as antifreeze, oil, filters, stabilizer and parts are billed separately, and we never do extra work without an estimate first.

boatclub.q: What is Big Water Boat Club?
boatclub.a: A membership that gives you access to Lake Texoma boat rentals at a big discount. Instead of the normal rental rate, members pay {club.discount}% of the posted rate at Lighthouse Resort & Marina.

boatclub.q: How much does it cost to join?
boatclub.a: The initiation fee is ${club.returningInitiation}, discounted to ${club.initiation} for your first membership, plus ${club.monthly} a month, billed quarterly (${club.quarterly}). After that, every boat you book at Lighthouse Resort & Marina is {club.discount}% off the posted rental rate.

boatclub.q: What do I need to join?
boatclub.a: Be {club.minAge} or older, pay the ${club.initiation} initiation fee and your first quarter’s dues (${club.quarterly}), complete the boater safety course at boaters-ed.com, and take the free Intro to Boating on Lake Texoma class from our partner BoaterWise.

boatclub.q: When can I rent a boat? How many reservations can I have?
boatclub.a: There are no restrictions or blackout dates. Rent half days, full days, weekdays, weekends and holidays. Book online or by phone, up to the day of your rental, subject to availability.

boatclub.q: How is Big Water Boat Club different from other boat clubs?
boatclub.a: Many clubs have high buy-ins, expensive monthly fees, membership tiers and reservation limits. Ours is simple: ${club.initiation} to join, ${club.monthly} a month, and {club.discount}% off rentals, plus discounts with affiliated companies and a professional team to help you make the most of every trip.

No. After you join you pay quarterly dues and {club.discount}% of the posted rental rate when you rent. Rates vary by season, weekday or weekend, and holidays: a winter half day at ${club.winterHalfDay} costs a member ${club.winterHalfDayHalf}, and a holiday full day of up to ${club.holidayFullDay} costs a member up to ${club.holidayHalfDay}. Each rental needs a refundable ${club.deposit} damage deposit on a major credit card, and you pay for the fuel you use at the discounted member rate.

Dues are billed quarterly, so the minimum commitment is three months, and you can cancel anytime after that with written notice. If you cancel and rejoin later, the initiation fee is ${club.returningInitiation}.

boatclub.q: Can I buy a boat later?
boatclub.a: Yes. The Member-to-Owner program helps members move into ownership when they’re ready, with Big Water Marine’s sales and service team behind them.

financing.q: What do I need to apply?
financing.a: The standard information any marine lender asks for: identification, income, and details of the boat you’re buying. The application is online and secure, and you’ll usually hear back quickly.
Yes. Repowering an existing boat can be financed the same way as a purchase, which often makes a new engine cheaper per month than continuing to repair an old one.
Yes. Terms vary by the age and value of the boat, so the best step is to apply and let us match you to the right lender.

financing.q: What about commercial or fleet purchases?

keepboating.q: Should I rent, join Big Water Boat Club, or buy a boat on Lake Texoma?
keepboating.a: It depends on how many days you boat. At about 1–3 days a year, renting keeps it simple. From roughly 2–9 days, Big Water Boat Club saves 50% on every rental for $500 to join and $150 a quarter. At 10 or more days a year, owning your own boat usually makes the most sense. Use the Rent, Join, Own calculator on this page to run your own numbers.

keepboating.q: Can I buy the boat I rented?
keepboating.a: Yes. Previous renters get exclusive discounts on our rental fleet boats, and last year’s boats are offered at big discounts. Same boat, same memories, and no more sold-out weekends.

keepboating.q: How much does Big Water Boat Club save on rentals?
keepboating.a: Members pay 50% of the posted rental rate at Lighthouse Resort & Marina, plus priority booking and access to member-only boats. With a $500 initiation (discounted from $1,000 for your first membership) and $50 a month billed quarterly, most members break even after about two rentals.

keepboating.q: Can I use a renter discount on a new boat?
keepboating.a: Yes. Apply your renter discount to any in-stock model when you buy new, with financing available.

storage.q: Is your storage indoor or outdoor?
storage.a: Outdoor only. We do not offer indoor or covered storage. Boats are kept in secure onsite outdoor storage at our Pottsboro location, and we recommend shrink wrap for anything staying through the winter.

storage.q: How do I get storage included?
storage.a: Our SecurePro winterization package ($1,750 onsite, labor for single-engine boats) includes six months of onsite secure outdoor storage, shrink wrap for boats up to 25 feet, and spring dewinterization.

storage.q: Can I store a boat without buying a winterization package?
storage.a: Call us. Standalone storage depends on current space, which is seasonal and fills up. 903-419-1019 is the fastest way to find out what’s open.
Yes. Shrink wrap is included for boats up to 25 feet in the SecurePro package and is available separately. It’s the single best protection for a boat stored outdoors through a Texoma winter.

storage.q: Can you pick up and deliver my boat?
storage.a: Pickup and delivery options are available. Tell us where the boat is — home, marina or storage facility — and we’ll quote it.

Dewinterization, or spring startup, gets the boat ready to run. It is included in the SecurePro package and available separately at $165 onsite or $215 mobile. It is also required to keep our winterization guarantee valid.

brands.q: Which brands do you sell new?
brands.a: Berkshire and Veranda pontoons, Scout center consoles, and Highfield rigid inflatable boats and tenders. All four are available new at our Pottsboro location.

brands.q: Which brand is best for Lake Texoma?
brands.a: It depends on how you boat. Pontoons suit entertaining and family days in Texoma chop; a Scout center console suits serious fishing; a Highfield RIB suits tenders and fast, rough-water runs. Come tell us how you use the lake.

brands.q: Do you sell used boats from other brands?

brands.q: Can I sea trial before I buy?
brands.a: Yes, by appointment. Schedule a demo and feel how the boat handles real Texoma water before you commit.

buyingGuide.q: What size boat is best for Lake Texoma?
buyingGuide.a: For most families, 22 to 25 feet. That range carries a crowd, handles afternoon chop, and still trailers and stores easily. Smaller boats are fine for calm mornings but get uncomfortable when the wind comes up.

buyingGuide.q: Are pontoons safe on a lake this big?
buyingGuide.a: Yes, when they are specified for it. A tritoon with a performance package handles Texoma chop well. A basic two-tube boat is better suited to sheltered water and calm mornings.
On Texoma, tritoon. The third tube adds buoyancy, stability and the ability to carry more power, which together make the difference on a windy afternoon.

buyingGuide.q: What is the best boat for striper fishing here?
buyingGuide.a: A 21 to 24 foot center console. The deep-V entry softens wind chop, and the open deck lets you follow a fish around the boat instead of over the furniture.

buyingGuide.q: Can I see a boat on the water before buying?
buyingGuide.a: Yes, by appointment. Call 903-419-1019 and we will schedule a demo. We would rather you find out on our time than after delivery.

newVsUsed.q: Is it cheaper to own a used boat on Lake Texoma?
newVsUsed.a: Up front, yes. Over a season, less than people expect. Winterization, shrink wrap and storage are priced by length rather than age, so they cost the same on either boat. The real variable is unplanned repairs.

newVsUsed.q: How much does it cost to store a boat for the winter?
newVsUsed.a: Secure outdoor storage is $2 per foot per month for shrinkwrapped boats, and wrap is $25 per foot. A 22-foot boat stored six months comes to about $814 for wrap and storage combined.

newVsUsed.q: Do I have to winterize on Lake Texoma?
newVsUsed.a: Yes, if you want to avoid a cracked block. Our packages start at $335 onsite, and our Guaranteed Winterization means that if your engine does not start in spring because of our process, we make it right at no charge.

newVsUsed.q: Are ex-rental boats a bad buy?
newVsUsed.a: Not necessarily. Fleet boats are maintained on a commercial schedule by factory-authorized technicians, so their service history is usually better documented than a private owner’s. Condition matters more than the badge.

newVsUsed.q: What costs do you not publish?
newVsUsed.a: Insurance, fuel, registration and slip fees, because they depend on your boat’s value, how you use it and who you insure with. Everything we control — service, winterization, storage, detailing — is published rather than quoted after the fact.

faqs.q: Where is Big Water Marine located?
faqs.a: Two locations in Pottsboro, Texas on Lake Texoma. Boat sales are at 50055 N State Hwy 289, open Tuesday through Saturday, 9am–5pm. Service is at 33 Tackle Box Dr, open Tuesday through Friday 8am–5pm and Saturday 8am–3pm. Both reach us at 903-419-1019.

faqs.q: What boat brands do you sell?
faqs.a: Four new brands: Berkshire and Veranda pontoons, Scout center consoles, and Highfield aluminum-hull RIBs and tenders. Boats are rigged with Suzuki, Yamaha, Mercury and Rotax power. Used inventory rotates and has included Trifecta, Carolina Skiff, Monterey and Sea Ray.

faqs.q: Do you sell used boats?
faqs.a: Yes. Used and brokerage boats are listed alongside new inventory, including gently used fleet and rental boats that have been maintained on a commercial service schedule. Current stock is on our inventory page with prices, photos and specs.

faqs.q: Do you take trade-ins?
faqs.a: Yes. We’ll appraise your boat, and final value is confirmed after an in-person inspection. If you’re replacing several boats at once, we’ll also tell you honestly whether trading or retailing them puts more money back in your pocket.

faqs.q: Do you offer financing?
faqs.a: Yes, for retail boat purchases and for repowers, through our lending partners. Applications are handled online. Commercial and fleet purchases don’t run through our retail lenders — for those we’ll help you find the right banking partner.

faqs.q: Will you service an engine you didn’t sell me?
faqs.a: Yes. We service all major outboard brands plus sterndrive and inboard/outboard setups, regardless of where the boat was bought. We’re a factory-authorized service center for Mercury, Yamaha, Suzuki and BRP, so warranty-approved work stays intact.

faqs.q: Do you come to my dock?
faqs.a: Yes. Mobile service brings a certified technician to your dock or marina, which is often the difference between losing a weekend and keeping it. Same-day service is available for routine maintenance. Call 903-419-1019 to schedule.

faqs.q: How much does winterization cost?
faqs.a: Onsite packages start at $335 for FreezeGuard, our essential freeze-protection service, and run to $1,750 for SecurePro, which adds shrink wrap, six months of storage and spring startup. All quotes are labor for single-engine boats; materials are additional, and mobile service is quoted separately.

faqs.q: What is Guaranteed Winterization?
faqs.a: If your engine doesn’t start in spring because of our winterization process, we make it right at no charge. It’s the reason we’d rather do the job properly in autumn than argue about it in April.

faqs.q: Do you offer boat storage?
faqs.a: Yes. Storage is available and is included for six months in our SecurePro winterization package, along with shrink wrap for boats up to 25 feet. Pickup and delivery options are available. Call for current availability, which is seasonal.

faqs.q: What is Big Water Boat Club?
faqs.a: A membership that gives you access to boats on Lake Texoma without owning one — no maintenance, storage or winterizing. Members book the boat they want and we handle the rest.

faqs.q: Do you sell boats to marinas and rental operators?
faqs.a: Yes. Fleet pricing starts at two boats, gets deeper at four, and reaches wholesale at eight. Delivery anywhere on Lake Texoma is included. We also service fleets at your dock, whether or not you bought the boats from us.

faqs.q: Is the trailer included in the price?
faqs.a: All of our boat packages include the trailer unless otherwise specified. If you don’t need one, we can remove it from the estimate.

faqs.q: What fees are not included in the listed price?
faqs.a: Tax, title and license (TTL), freight, prep and doc fee are not reflected in the posted price. We’ll walk you through the full out-the-door number before you commit to anything.

faqs.q: Can I sea trial a boat before buying?
faqs.a: Yes, by appointment. Contact sales to schedule an on-water demo so you can feel how the boat handles Texoma chop before you decide.
